turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Hi, Dr. [name]. Well, I'm a barber, and I'm here because I've gotten to the point where I'll do almost anything to avoid using the straight razor at work. I'll switch clients with my coworkers, or I'll just say the blade is missing, or I'll even hide it in the drawer. And if I absolutely can't get out of doing a straight razor shave, I'm just shaking through the whole thing. It's gotten really bad.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient describes actively avoiding the straight razor through various tactics (switching clients, hiding blades) and enduring the situation with severe physical distress ('shaking through the whole thing') when avoidance is impossible.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel that fear about using the straight razor, is it more that you're afraid of the blade itself, or are you having unwanted thoughts or images about accidentally hurting your client with it?
turns.patient_response: I guess it's more about hurting someone. I mean, I know it's just a tool that I trained with, and I can use clippers all day long without any issue. But when that straight razor is just sitting open at my station, it really feels like I'm about to hurt somebody, or even cut myself badly. So yeah, it's that feeling of causing a bad cut.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient describes marked, disproportionate fear focused specifically on having an open straight razor at their station, experiencing an intense feeling that they will hurt someone or cut themselves despite knowing it is just a tool they trained with.

turns.doctor_question: Do these thoughts about accidentally cutting or hurting someone ever pop into your mind even when you're not at work or near a razor, or are they only triggered when the blade is actually in front of you?
turns.patient_response: No, it's really only when I'm at the shop or right in front of one. I don't just sit at home having thoughts about it out of nowhere. It's a very immediate thing—the second I hear a client ask for a razor shave, or if I see the blade flipped open, it just hits me. My chest tightens up, my hands get sweaty, and... it’s like my body just wants to physically back away before I can even think.

symptom_reasoning.S063: The patient describes an immediate fear and anxiety reaction with physical symptoms (chest tightening, sweaty hands) the moment a razor is mentioned or seen.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from avoiding or hiding the razor, do you ever feel the urge to check things repeatedly, perform a certain ritual, or do something in a specific way to make sure you haven't hurt anyone?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I don't do any routines or rituals like that. I mean, I don't need to check if I haven't used the razor, you know? I just try to avoid it completely. Once I get out of doing the shave and the blade is put away, I know everyone is safe, so I don't go back and check on the client or do anything special. I just move on to the next haircut.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly denies engaging in checking behaviors, routines, or rituals to ensure safety.
